questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
What is a characteristic of a merit good?

options.A: free at the point of use
options.B: has zero marginal costs
options.C: non-competitive in use
options.D: possesses positive externality

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct?

options.A: External benefit minus private benefit equals social benefit.
options.B: Private benefit minus external benefit equals social benefit.
options.C: Social benefit minus external benefit equals private benefit.
options.D: Social benefit plus private benefit equals external benefit.

questions.questionText: When does a consumer achieve maximum total utility (TU), according to marginal utility (MU) theory for two goods, X and Y, with different prices (P)?

options.A: MU = MU X Y MU MU
options.B: X = Y P P X Y MU MU
options.C: X = Y P P Y X
options.D: TU = TU X Y

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a change in a consumer’s budget line from RR to SS. R product Y S O R S product X What might explain why this occurred?

options.A: a decrease in income and a fall in the price of X
options.B: a decrease in income and a rise in the price of X
options.C: an increase in income and a fall in the price of X
options.D: an increase in income and a rise in the price of X

questions.questionText: When shirts are produced, fixed costs are $100 and the variable cost is $5 per shirt. If the price is $10, which output would result in normal profit?

options.A: 10 shirts
options.B: 20 shirts
options.C: 25 shirts
options.D: 100 shirts

questions.questionText: The table shows four market structures. Which characteristics could describe the market structure shown? barriers differentiated market structure to entry products

options.A: monopolistic competition low no
options.B: monopoly high yes
options.C: oligopoly low no
options.D: perfect competition high yes

questions.questionText: A firm abandons its policy of horizontal expansion and switches to a policy of backward vertical growth. What does this suggest is most likely about the firm’s objectives?

options.A: It now prefers revenue maximisation to cost minimisation.
options.B: It now prefers sales maximisation to profit satisficing.
options.C: It now prefers security of sales to profit maximisation.
options.D: It now prefers security of supplies to growth of market share.

questions.questionText: What identifies the output level required to meet the stated aim of the firm? aim of firm produce at output where

options.A: maximum efficiency marginal cost is at a minimum
options.B: profit maximising marginal cost is equal to average revenue
options.C: quantity of sales maximising average revenue is equal to average cost
options.D: revenue maximising marginal revenue is zero

questions.questionText: What makes it likely that firms will collude in setting prices for a particular product?

options.A: a highly contestable market structure
options.B: a small number of firms with economies of scale
options.C: persistent shortages of the product being supplied
options.D: the existence of patent rights possessed by firms

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s marginal and average cost curves. The firm enters a collusive agreement with other firms in the industry. It is agreed that each firm will charge a common price, OP, and will restrict the level of its output to a production quota set by the industry cartel. The firm is allocated a production quota, Oq. $ MC AC G H P K L J M N O q quantity The firm decides to cheat in order to maximise its profits. What is its short-run increase in profits?

options.A: PGKL
options.B: PHJL
options.C: PHJL minus PGNM
options.D: PGKL minus LKNM

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a notice on a motorway near Cambridge. This road was recently cleared of 17 bags of litter. Clearing litter puts local authority road-workers’ lives at risk. What is this an example of?

options.A: government regulation
options.B: merit good
options.C: nudge theory
options.D: public good

questions.questionText: A reason for government intervention in the workings of the economy is to attempt to correct for market failure. Sometimes, though, government failure may occur. What is not a possible reason for government failure?

options.A: Governments may have to make decisions on the basis of out-of-date information.
options.B: Governments may make decisions that reduce negative externalities.
options.C: The extent of the market failure may be difficult to judge.
options.D: When circumstances change a government may be unable to respond quickly.

questions.questionText: Which policy combination will reduce income inequalities in a country?

options.A: impose a fixed amount tax on all people and reduce unemployment benefits
options.B: increase social welfare payments and impose a higher marginal income tax rate
options.C: increase transfer payments and impose higher indirect taxation
options.D: reduce rates of tax on higher incomes and increase welfare payments

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an economy’s Lorenz curve (VW). 100 W 45° cumulative % of income area Y area Z V 0 100 cumulative % of population How is the Gini coefficient for the economy calculated? Y Y Z Z

options.A: B C D Y+Z Z Y Y+Z

questions.questionText: What will cause the supply curve of labour in a particular industry to shift to the left?

options.A: a fall in demand for the industry’s product
options.B: a greater use of machinery in the production of the industry’s output
options.C: a rise in wages paid in similar occupations in other industries
options.D: a weakening of trade union influence in the industry

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the costs and revenue curves in the labour market for a firm in imperfect competition. $ MC L W W AC L W W ARP
A country has a population of 100 million. 60 million are of working age and 50 million are in the labour force. The country’s unemployment rate is 10%. How many people are employed?

options.A: 40 million B 45 million C 50 million D 54 million

questions.questionText: The table shows the nominal GDP growth and inflation rate in four countries, W, X, Y and Z. nominal GDP annual inflation growth rate (%) rate (%) W 2.1 1.9 X –1.6 8.9 Y 4.1 5.8 Z –2.0 16.4 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: W experienced the highest rate of real economic growth.
options.B: X and Z experienced deflation.
options.C: Y experienced the greatest rise in the standard of living.
options.D: Z experienced the greatest growth in public debt.

questions.questionText: Which trade policy of a developed country is least likely to allow a developing country to experience increased growth?

options.A: a decrease in administrative restrictions on imports from developing countries
options.B: an increase in subsidies of capital goods exports to developing countries
options.C: a reduction in quotas on imports from developing countries
options.D: a reduction in tariffs on imports from developing countries

questions.questionText: What is not included in National Income accounts?

options.A: a gift by a parent to her daughter as a deposit on an apartment
options.B: earnings of a part-time worker in a school dining room
options.C: interest earned on savings accounts intended for retirement
options.D: profits re-invested by a company to fund capital expenditure

questions.questionText: A developing country relies heavily on the production of a primary product for its national income. Which change will make it more likely that the country will benefit from its participation in international trade?

options.A: an increase in income elasticity of demand for the primary product
options.B: an increase in tariffs imposed on the primary product by developed countries
options.C: an increase in the cost of international freight transport in real terms
options.D: an increase in the price of manufactured products relative to the primary product

questions.questionText: What might cause a country to experience both a rise in the number of people unemployed and an increase in job vacancies?

options.A: a decrease in housing and transport costs
options.B: a decrease in unemployment benefit
options.C: an increase in the occupational immobility of labour
options.D: an increase in the skills of the labour force

questions.questionText: In a two sector economy autonomous consumption expenditure increases by $100 billion, autonomous investment expenditure by $200 billion and the marginal propensity to consume is 0.5. What will be the increase in National Income?

options.A: $150 billion
options.B: $300 billion
options.C: $450 billion
options.D: $600 billion

questions.questionText: The central bank in an open economy cuts the interest rate to avoid deflation. Under which conditions is this expansionary monetary policy most likely to be effective? asset prices consumption spending

options.A: rise rapidly interest elastic
options.B: rise rapidly interest inelastic
options.C: rise slowly interest elastic
options.D: rise slowly interest inelastic

questions.questionText: The diagram shows that the elasticity of demand for money becomes infinite at a certain rate of interest. rate of interest demand for money O quantity of money Which statement explains this situation?

options.A: At low interest rates there is an infinite demand for bonds.
options.B: Other assets are close substitutes for money.
options.C: Some money is required for transactions balances.
options.D: There is a liquidity trap.

questions.questionText: What would be most likely to result in an increase in unemployment?

options.A: a decrease in the level of bank loans
options.B: a decrease in the level of taxation
options.C: a decrease in the rate of interest
options.D: an increase in the money supply

questions.questionText: Which macroeconomic indicator is least likely to identify a developing country?

options.A: real GDP per capita
options.B: the Gini coefficient
options.C: the Human Development Index
options.D: the Phillips curve

questions.questionText: What would not help to achieve the macroeconomic objective of economic growth?

options.A: decreasing corporation tax
options.B: increasing income tax
options.C: reducing interest rates
options.D: spending on education and training

questions.questionText: What is a reflationary fiscal measure?

options.A: increasing government spending
options.B: increasing taxes
options.C: increasing the money supply
